objective: Verify current standards and durable implementation patterns before building the Book-parent immutable version and rollback boundary, without replacing existing Book canonical-state authority or importing a generic event-sourcing platform.
existing_parent_law_preserved: author decisions remain explicit objects and cannot be synthesized by rollback
publication and export-freeze authority remain separate from technical state restoration

sources.finding: JSON Schema 2020-12 remains the current published JSON Schema dialect and is appropriate for deterministic contract/fixture validation where JSON Schema is used.

Git commit objects represent a snapshot in time and bind parent commit object IDs; this is a useful conceptual model for immutable Book snapshots and predecessor lineage, but Git itself is not selected as the Book runtime database.

Git models committed history as snapshots and references rather than destructive in-place historical edits; this supports the Book rule that restoration creates a new current successor instead of rewriting an old state.

PostgreSQL supports SERIALIZABLE transactions and reports serialization_failure when concurrent behavior cannot be represented as a serial execution; a future database-backed implementation may use this or equivalent compare-and-swap protection rather than silent merge.
Database rollback/savepoint semantics are transaction controls for uncommitted work. They do not justify deleting or rewriting already committed Book historical versions.

Persisting an outbox record in the same local transaction as the aggregate change avoids a committed-state/unpublished-event split; consumers must remain idempotent because relays can publish more than once.

decisions.decision: Every committed Book parent state is an immutable snapshot with exact state_version, state_digest, predecessor_state_version and predecessor_state_digest. Historical snapshots are never modified in place.

Every changed versioned parent object creates a new immutable object-version node with exact payload digest and predecessor version reference. Reusing an existing object-version identity with different bytes fails closed.

Rollback is implemented as RESTORE_AS_NEW_SUCCESSOR: read a historical target, revalidate it against current governance/evidence requirements, then commit a new current snapshot whose restored pointers/content are explicitly derived from that historical target. The current pointer never moves backward to mutate history.

Every mutation/restore requires exact expected current state_version and state_digest. A persistent SQL adapter should use one local transaction with SERIALIZABLE or equivalent conditional-write semantics; serialization/conflict failures are retried only as a newly revalidated request, never silently merged.

The new state snapshot, version-ledger receipt and any outbox entry form one logical transaction. If any part fails, none become current. Outbox delivery is outside canonical authority and must be idempotent.

A restore must revalidate current rights/privacy, dependency currentness, unresolved critical evidence and required author decisions. Historical approval cannot be treated as current approval merely because it existed in the target snapshot.

RESTORE_CONTENT never restores EXPORT_FROZEN or PUBLISHED_OR_DELIVERED status. RESTORE_FULL_STATE may reproduce a historical workflow status only after current exact export/artifact and author-publication evidence is explicitly revalidated; otherwise the request fails closed.
A future SQL adapter may use savepoints internally for bounded sub-operations, but savepoint behavior is not the canonical Book version model and does not alter committed historical identity.
Use JSON Schema 2020-12 semantics for externalized schemas/fixtures where useful, while keeping the executable core deterministic and fail-closed even if no third-party schema package is present.
Use Git's immutable snapshot/parent-lineage model only as design evidence. Do not make Git branches/commits the Book application's canonical runtime state database.
The Book need is immutable version history plus transactional receipts/outbox, not a new general event-sourcing/CQRS subsystem.

No distributed multi-service rollback is required for the current parent-local version boundary. If a later workflow spans independently committed services, research that separately rather than overbuilding now.

implementation_contract.current_pointer: Exactly one current snapshot identity; historical snapshots remain addressable by exact version+digest.
implementation_contract.transaction_rule: State snapshot + version receipt + outbox entry commit atomically as one logical transaction.

exact_next_action: Define BOOK-SYSTEM-VERSION-AND-ROLLBACK-001 contract and implement one deterministic parent-owned executable core plus adversarial fixtures and hosted prequalification.
qualification_effect: NONE. Research decisions do not qualify executable bytes or grant canonical, author, publication, production, Prose or document-engine authority.
